processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles with solidification in Cu moulds, followed by Bridgman monocrystal growth
processing_steps.duration: about 12 h (crystal growth with subsequent cooling)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Binary Fe-Al alloys were prepared by vacuum induction melting in Al2O3 crucibles using Fe of 99.99% purity (zone-melted) and Al of 99.999% purity, with solidification in Cu moulds to rods usually 18 mm diameter. Monocrystals with up to 10 cm length were grown by the Bridgman method (10–15 mm/h pulling rate); the crystal growth with subsequent cooling occurred within about 12 h. The monocrystals were etched by ammonium persulfate and oriented using a laser light-figure method.

processing_steps.method: electrostatic discharge machining, mechanical polishing, ultrasonic cleansing in acetone
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimens were cut by electrostatic discharge machining, mechanically polished and cleansed by ultrasound in acetone (except for the monocrystals). Monocrystal surfaces were polished with 3 µm diamond paste before testing.

processing_steps.atmosphere: enclosed in evacuated (10^-6 bar) SiO2 capsule
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The specimens were heat-treated at temperatures up to 600 °C usually for less than 14 days, at higher temperatures less than 4 days and at 1100 °C usually only 15 min. For heat treatments above 300 °C the specimens were enclosed in evacuated (10^-6 bar) SiO2 capsules; no Si uptake was detected.

processing_steps.method: furnace cooling from 1100 °C to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: 1100 °C FC RT denotes furnace cooling from 1100 °C to room temperature. This is the terminal heat-treatment state defining the sample (minimum-degree-of-order / near-equilibrium vacancy state).

structures.overall_structure: Single-crystal (monocrystalline) Fe-16%Al; no grain boundaries. The same Fe-16%Al monocrystal type was studied (111)-oriented for the microhardness measurements and [112]-oriented for the compressive stress-strain measurements. Contains rare globular AlN inclusions. No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C.
structures.number_of_phases: 1 matrix phase (Fe-Al solid solution) plus rare AlN inclusions

phases_present.phase_name: Fe-Al solid solution (bcc Fe-Al matrix; degree of short-range order depends on heat treatment, minimum ordering after furnace cooling/quenching from high temperature)
phases_present.texture: (111) orientation used for hardness specimens; [112] orientation used for compression specimens

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: not applicable (single crystal, no grain boundaries)

precipitates.distribution: rare, globular inclusions dispersed in the monocrystal

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Fischerscope H100 microhardness tester, maximum load 1 N; HU averages of more than 40 measurements

hardness.region: 1100 °C FC RT (furnace cooling from 1100 °C to room temperature), (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal
hardness.uncertainty: data vary only by about 10% at most; the 1100 °C FC RT condition scatters tightly about the 2000 N/mm² gridline

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: compression testing; yield stress determined as 0.2% proof stress

stress_strain_curves.description: compressive stress-strain curve at room temperature, 10^-4 s^-1: rises steeply through a knee at roughly 1.5–2% strain, then continues as a nearly flat plateau with slight hardening, running low over most of the strain range and ending in the 470–480 MPa band at about 5.5% strain

stress_strain_distribution.description: Prior heat treatment changes the flow stress of these monocrystals only modestly; the 1100 °C FC condition lies at the low end of the four curves (plateau/end stress ~470–480 MPa at ~5.5% strain).

characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-16%Al monocrystal: real Al 16.0 at.% (8.4 wt.-%), C 45 wt.ppm, Si 40 wt.ppm, O 60 wt.ppm.

characterization_methods.technique: optical microscopy after etching (alcoholic 10% nitric acid)
characterization_methods.purpose: metallographic inspection for grain boundaries and precipitates
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to reveal precipitates/inclusions; no carbides detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C.

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis
characterization_methods.purpose: studying fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate/inclusion analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: Rare globular AlN inclusions (diameters up to 30 µm) identified in the monocrystals by EDX.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Fischerscope H100 microhardness tester, maximum load 1 N
characterization_methods.purpose: determination of elastic and plastic deformation / hardness
characterization_methods.key_findings: HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]; values are averages of more than 40 measurements; HU of the 1100 °C FC RT monocrystal ≈2000 N/mm².

characterization_methods.purpose: determination of yield stress / stress-strain behaviour
characterization_methods.key_findings: Compressive stress-strain curves of the [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal after 1100 °C FC showed only modest effect of heat treatment.

unmapped_findings: Short-range ordering in Fe-Al alloys with 13–18 at.% Al occurs at temperatures below 600 °C during cooling after solidification; the highest degree of short-range ordering was observed at 250 °C (isochronal anneals of Fe-18%Al for 14 days), with an activation energy of only 0.3 eV/atom, and quenching from 1100 °C suppressed short-range ordering nearly completely.

For the heat-treated Fe-16%Al monocrystal specimens, the various treatments produce different states of short-range order (maximum after 250 °C/14 day anneal, minimum after quenching from 1100 or 600 °C); the 250 °C/14 day anneal for maximum ordering, the quench from 600 °C, furnace cooling from 1100 °C to room temperature and anneals at 300 °C for 6 h and 3 days all produce the same hardness, equal to that of the as-grown monocrystal. It is concluded that short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness.

The vacancy formation enthalpy for Fe-Al alloys with 16–18% Al is about 1–1.2 eV, so a high concentration of excess vacancies is expected after quenching from 1100 °C; excess vacancies are immobile at low temperatures and act as effective obstacles to dislocation movement (vacancy hardening).

Only heat treatments at temperatures above 600 °C affect the mechanical behaviour of the Fe-Al alloys significantly; the 1100 °C FC RT condition therefore represents a heat treatment that affects behaviour only modestly (HU varies by only about 5–10% around 2000 N/mm²).
